The petitioner has filed this petition assailing the order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1) passed in Execution Case No.101/2020 by the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum Chhatarpur,
District-Chhatarpur.
2. It is contended by the counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner herein had moved a complaint under Section 12 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 before the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Chhatarpur.

sentences.text: 3. The said complaint was controverted by the Insurance Company i.e. respondent herein.
The Consumer Forum then passed an order dated 10.08.2020 (Annexure P/4) and held that the present petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,60,910/- towards compensation.
As the order passed by Forum was not being complied with, the present petitioner herein submitted an application for execution.
The said application was registered as Execution Case No.101/2020 before the Executing Court.

An objection was taken by the respondent herein that as the present petitioner had claimed total loss, the registration of the vehicle was required to be cancelled in terms of Section 55 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
It was the objection by the respondent before the Forum that such statutory requirement being sine qua non was required to be fulfilled before the execution of the award.

4 . The said objection submitted by the respondent was entertained by the Forum and the Forum vide impugned order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1), directed the present petitioner to submit the cancellation of registration in terms of Section 55 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

5. The counsel submits that the impugned order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1) passed by District Consumer Forum is contrary to law inasmuch as, it is not within the jurisdiction of Executing Court as the Executing Court, being incompetent cannot pass over-reach the original order.
It is contended by the counsel that Executing Court has travelled beyond the jurisdiction vested in it by law.

Thus,
counsel submits that the impugned order deserves to be quashed.

6. Per contra, counsel for the respondent submits that the present petition before this Court directly is not maintainable inasmuch as, there is an alternative and efficacious remedy exists in Section 72 of the Consumer Protection Act and therefore, this petition is not maintainable.

It is contended by the counsel for the respondent that out of the total amount of compensation, an amount of Rs.4,50,000/- has already been paid to the present petitioner and the remaining amount of Rs.48,487/- shall be paid once when the cancellation of registration certificate is submitted by the petitioner in terms of the order passed by the Forum in Execution Case No.101/2020.

It is further contended by the counsel that even otherwise the order passed by the Forum is innocuous and also is in conformity with the statutory provisions contained in Section 55 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988, therefore, no interference is warranted.
7.
Heard the rival submission of both the parties and perused the record.

8. Firstly to deal with the objection regarding the alternative remedy, Section 71 provides for enforcement of the order passed by District Commission and in terms of the said provisions, an order passed by the District Commission is executed in the same manner as a decree made by Civil Court is executed in terms of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Section 72 provides that if there is failure by any party to comply with the order of District Commission, he can be punished with imprisonment for a term which is not be less than one moth but which may extend to three years.
An order passed under Section 72 (2) is appealable under Section 73 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

Apart from an order which is passed under Section 72 (1), there is no remedy Rishi Prakash Birthare vs The New India Insurance Company on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157663106/
2 of appeal against any order under the aforesaid Section 73 of Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As in the present case, the order impugned has not been passed under Section 72 (1) of Consumer Protection Act, 2019, thus the remedy of appeal under Section 73 is not available to the present petitioner.
Hence, the preliminary objection, stands rejected.
9. The impugned order is passed by the Forum in execution case where the execution of order dated 10.08.2020 (Annexure P/4) is being sought.

In the order dated 10.08.2020 passed by the District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Chhatarpur, there is no direction by the Forum as regards cancellation of registration of vehicle in concerned in terms of Section 55 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988.
10.

entities.text: District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Chhatarpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is also evident from perusal of the order dated 10.08.2020 (Annexure P/4) that it was not the stand of the respondent/insurance company in reply to original complaint that there should have been cancellation of registration in terms of Section 55 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
The Forum passed an unconditional order directing the respondent to pay the compensation amount of Rs.4,60,910/-.
The said order was passed by the Forum was made subject matter of execution proceedings.

In the execution, the impugned order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1) was passed and in the execution case, the Forum observed that if the petitioner herein submits certificate regarding cancellation of vehicle registration, the remaining amount of compensation of Rs.48,487/- shall be paid to the present petitioner.
The said condition regarding submission of cancellation of registration certificate was not there in order dated 10.08.2020, therefore, the Executing Court has travelled beyond the original order.

It is trite that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree but in the present case, while dealing with the execution case, a condition has been imposed by the impugned order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1) which is not available in the order dated 10.08.2020 (Annexure P/4).
11. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 09.11.2020 (Annexure P/1) is quashed.

The District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Chhatarpur, District- Chhatarpur is directed to take final decision in the Execution Case No.101/2020 within a period of 90 days from the date of production of certified copy of the order passed today.

entities.text: District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, Chhatarpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 12. With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed.
